recipes.name: Egg and Hash Brown Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (20 ounce) package frozen O'Brien hashbrown potatoes, thawed
1 (12 ounce) package bulk pork breakfast sausage

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Toss potatoes with vegetable oil in a bowl until potatoes are well coated. Press potatoes into a 10-inch pie pan to create a crust.
Bake potatoes in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 30 minutes. Remove pan from oven and reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

While potatoes are baking, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir in sausage. Cook and stir until sausage is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease. Combine sausage with eggs, mushrooms, pepper jack cheese, Swiss cheese, milk, 1 tablespoon parsley, garlic salt, and black pepper in a large bowl. Pour egg mixture into the prepared potato crust.

Bake in the oven until eggs are set, about 25 minutes. Arrange tomato slices over eggs and sprinkle the remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons parsley on top. Return to the oven and continue baking until tomatoes soften, about 5 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Egg and Hash Brown Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Use crispy potatoes to make a delicious crust for this cheesy sausage, egg, and hash brown breakfast casserole recipe that the whole family will love!

video.description: Impress brunch guests with this delicious and nutritious breakfast casserole. Begin by baking a golden crust out of hash brown potatoes, then fill with sausage, eggs, fresh mushrooms, pepperjack and Swiss cheeses. Finish off with garlic salt, chopped fresh parsley and thin slices of fresh tomato. The color, freshness and textures will win over your group, and the easiness of this recipe will have you returning again and again.

review.reviewBody: just made this recipe tonight and it is AMAZING! i followed the recipe almost exactly as written, but i only had a 9 1/2 inch pie pan, i upped the mushrooms (kind of on accident but i like it!) and covered the top with tomatoes. also, at the very end, i put the broiler on just for a few minutes to finish off the tomatoes. i highly highly recommend this recipe and will definitely be doing it again very soon! YUM! thanks, ddelisle!

Delicious! I had to make many changes based on what I had available, and this recipe allowed me to do that and still produce a great meal: I used a 28oz bag of potatoes O’Brien; since this was a spur of the moment undertaking I split the bag onto two dinner plates and cooked each one in the microwave on high for 3-4 minutes to thaw. Tossed the thawed potatoes 1/4 cup canola oil and lightly pressed them into a 9x13 glass baking dish. After 20 minutes in the oven the potatoes weren’t browning, so I sprayed a light layer of cooking spray on top. Although the spray didn’t help the potatoes brown, the overspray that coated the sides of the baking dish helped the egg/sausage/cheese mixture to not stick and cleanup was very easy. After 30 minutes the potatoes still hadn’t browned, but this turned out to be no problem at all. While potatoes were baking I cooked a 12oz roll of sage sausage and added 3/4 of a medium yellow onion, diced, to the sausage when it was 2/3 of the way done. Drained that to get rid of extra grease. At the advice of other reviewers I used 12 eggs instead of six to which I added salt, pepper, 1 tsp each garlic powder, ground mustard, and cayenne pepper, and 3/4 cup of 2% milk. Added the sausage/onion mixture to the eggs and then incorporated an 8oz bag of finely shredded mild cheddar. Spread the mixture on top of the potatoes and baked at 350 for 30 minutes. Added sliced tomatoes to the top and broiled for 2 minutes. Despite all of the changes this was amazing.

My favorite aspect of this recipe is the hash browns crust.
I regularly cook brunch casseroles for our group brunches and adding the hash browns crust brought a novel change to my regular egg based casserole.
For our group, I scaled-up to a 10.5" x 14.75" (4 Qt) dish.
I used 9 eggs instead of the suggested 6 eggs. The crust required about 30 oz. of hash browns ( 1 1/2 bags). For the filling I first fried about 6 slices (chopped-up) of bacon. I then removed the bacon and drained most of the grease. Then I added 1lb of ground sausage to the pan . When done, I removed the cook sausage adding it to the cooked bacon bits and sautéed onions, garlic, mushrooms. Add a little chicken broth or a bit of cream sherry. I also added 1 can of mild chili to add a little zest. The added liquid will deglaze the pan and add to the broth. Add seasoning to taste and add back the sausage and bacon. Reduce till most of the liquid is gone.
cover and add to the egg / cheese mixture.
Per the recipe, to the prepared hash brown crust add the eggs mixture. bake as described. Our brunch group was very happy with the result. Thank you for ideas!

This was delicious! Used a 9x13 pan to cook a 20oz bag of refrigerated hash browns. Didn't have the original recipe ingredients on hand so made the following changes. To make this vegetarian I used 2 chipotle field road meat alternative sausages. Threw in chopped asparagus and a red bell pepper with the eggs. When taking the hash browns out - I laid 6 slices of pepper jack cheese directly on the potatoes. Added the egg/veg mixture and baked an additional 30 minutes. This was so good - my husband kept going back for more. This recipe will definitely make it into our dinner rotation.

This was a fantastic and truly rich casserole! I used fresh grated potatoes, which are much cheaper than the packaged/frozen/sometime additive-laden hash browns. I ended up cooking in a cast iron 10" pan, heating it with the oven. Took 5 more minutes to cook the potatoes before adding the egg mixture. The tomatoes went right back in the oven with everything else and cooked perfectly in 30 minutes. Thanks so much for this awesome dish!

i was running late for dinner and couldn't find my 8x8 pan so used a muffin tin instead. this allowed a reduced cooking time about 15 min total for the egg/tomato stages. also didn't thaw the frozen potatoes, used a pound of sausage because that was the package size, used half the cheese - some good jalapeno pepper jack, no mushrooms. did add garlic salt to the potatoes as other suggested and a bit of cayenne pepper to the egg mixture and onions sauteed with the sausage. with the reduced time to cook the potatoes and the eggs, nothing was dry or crispy, but definitely a good breakfast for dinner option.

I made minor changes. I shredded raw potatoes, baked it in a 7x11-inch dish, reduced heat from 425 to 400 degrees since it was a glass dish but cooked the same amount of time. Used 12 oz. swiss & co-jack cheeses. Put about 8 oz. sliced cherry tomatoes on top. Made 11 servings @ 6 oz. I froze the leftovers. Note the recipe calls for 12 oz. sausage but sausage rolls come in 16 oz. packages.

I made this for a baby shower yesterday and it was a hit. I was so nervous to make this because I hate using new recipies for a party. I did make some changes. I used frozen hash potatoes and baked them in the casserole dish the night before. I also used smoked turkey sausage and sauteed them with peppers, green onions, and fresh garlic in a garlic and herb infused sunflower oil from Wegmans. The next morning I used 12 eggs, 1 cup of swiss cheese, and 1 cup of pepper jack cheese and poured it into the sausage mix. I added salt and pepper, then poured them into the prepared casserole dish. I had to bake mine for 60 minutes at 350. Not a piece left!

Mae this for this morning's brunch For 13 folks. Everyone liked it. I did make some changes. Put salt, pepper, and a little garlic powder on potatoes before cooking. Also used half reg and half hot pork sausage. Added onion to mushroom and sausage mix. Used 10 eggs and 3/4 C milk plus 1/4 Cup half-n-half since I cooked it in a 9x13" dish. Increased both cheeses to 1 Cup. Very good and pretty with tomatoes on top. Next time I'll serve with salsa on the side too!
This was really good, perfect for MOPS breakfasts. I cooked the potatoes in the dish the night before and used precooked sausage so there was less to do in the morning.

Very good. I added fried onions to the hash browns. Also sautéed onions (my husband loves onions in just about everything) and the mushrooms before adding to the eggs. I think I would add sour cream next time as suggested by another reviewer. I'd definitely make this recipe again
I used onions, I had no mushrooms, but I had a mushroom everything seasoning I used. I also top it with the cheese instead of mixing it in. DELICIOUS

I cooked it a bit longer so the centre was well cooked but as you can see the edges crisped up however it was very tasty. I even put some dehydrated tomatoes in it from my garden. Very tasty and a salad along side balanced it out nicely.
This is very tasty as written although I will tweak it a bit next time for personal taste. Thank you very much for sharing this recipe!

I think the recipe was tasty as is. I did add sauteed onion, small to it as well as diced ham, and the sausage was hot sausage. I added some basil to the egg. I had yellow peppers from my garden, diced up and added. Add no salt. the cheese has enough, Great recipe. Will make again

This recipe is very good. I prepared half the recipe and only had Italian sausage at hand so that is what I used. It came out perfect. I think this recipe may have benefited from 4 eggs rather than the 3 the recipe called for if halved. Will make it again! I made a side of the Cold Oven Popovers recipe from this site. I sprinkled some Swiss Cheese on top too. It was a fantastic combo!

I made this, this morning for a meeting at the Church, went down wonderfully. Thank you for the receipe.
next time I make it, will use more eggs!
It tasted very good, but was a lot of work. My husband was making a simpler version years ago using a large skillet and jokingly called it "Breakfast Mess".
So easy to make and fun to tweak. I went ‘south western’ and added chorizo and avocado. Yum!
I did not make any changes. We had it for supper. We enjoyed it and will make it again. I might switch out the sausage for ground beef for a change.
